title: P8: the spaces that user agents implement (design v2, plan decision 77). Step 1 (W1 and W5): the use-context of an agent and the write rule of an agent reference (SpaceRefs.v A1), the matcher state codec, the matcher process and the sink. Step 2 (W2 and W7): the call of a send on an agent space (TS-1 to TS-3) and the R7 replies to agent-minted names (SpaceRefs.v A2). Step 3 (W3 and W6): the translation of a receive (AgentTranslation.v A3 to A8) and the native consume of a handle. Step 4 (W4): the translation of `new`: the agent-minted names (SpaceRefs.v A9) and the resume term (AgentTranslation.v A10).
design: P8 design v2 (.reified-rspaces-work/p8/design-v2.md), sections 3, 4, 7 and 9. The headline ids are the ids of the P8 phase of formal/reified-rspaces-invariant-map.json. The agent routes of route (AG-1) re-prove the P4 headlines route_total_deterministic and route_rules, so the P4 map holds route, agent_parts and UseKind. The agent arms of single_target (P8 step 3, TR-1 and TR-2) re-prove the P5 headline query_source_routes_inner_channel, so the P5 map holds single_bind_route.
code_base: The items are in the P8 commits of this repository. The line numbers are informative. The checker finds each item by its scope and name.

A1.name: agent_ref_requires_write_flag
A1.statement: A use block enters the context of a user agent exactly when the evaluated reference has a call channel under the bundle rule of eval_send; under a bundle without the write flag it fails with HandleNotWritable.

A2.name: r7_agent_reply_bundle_exact
A2.statement: For every single bundle, the R7 backend makes the call on a user agent exactly when the bundle has both flags and its body is an agent-tagged tuple, with the agent and the raw channel of the tuple; every other bundle routes to the default space, as in HEAD (R7A-1).

A3.name: offsets_partition
A3.statement: The ranges [off_i, off_i + f_i) of the binds of a translated receive partition the binder positions [0, total): every position below total has exactly one owner bind (TR-3).

A4.name: env_keys_disjoint_union
A4.statement: The env keys of the binds of a translated receive are disjoint, and their union is the key set {0, ..., total - 1} of the map pattern of the body receive (MO-3, TR-6).

A5.name: body_equivalence
A5.statement: The body receive binds, in binder order, exactly the values that the native receive binds: the matched values of every bind in bind order (TR-6).

A6.name: guard_fold_sound
A6.statement: The guard of the owner bind of TR-4, over the placeholders of that bind, has the value of the native guard over the values of every bind, so the matcher filters as the native guard check does.

A7.name: matcher_sound_complete
A7.statement: The matcher op replies (true, env) exactly when the spatial match of the injected matcher succeeds and the guard of the bind passes, and env maps the global position of each binder of the bind to its value (MO-3).

A8.name: matcher_state_roundtrip
A8.statement: The codec of a matcher state is exact: a consistent state decodes from its encoding and from its matcher id, a decoded state re-encodes to the same bytes, and the encoding is injective (TR-5, MO-2).

A9.name: tag_untag_id
A9.statement: An agent-minted name is one bundle with both flags around the agent-tagged tuple of its agent and its raw channel: both bundle rules give the tuple, the tuple routes to its agent with its raw channel under every context (R4), and the R7 backend reads the same parts from the name (R7A-1) (TN-3).

A10.name: resume_binds_innermost
A10.statement: The resume term of a translated new binds every binder of the new in its order: each target evaluates to the bound name of its binder or to the agent-minted name of the reply of its rank, and BoundVar(k - 1 - j) reads binder j after the match, as in a native new (TN-3).

items.name: call_channel
items.role: The call channel of an agent under the bundle rule of eval_send (AG-4).

items.name: space_ref
items.role: Evaluate and classify a space reference; an agent reference must have a call channel (AG-4).

items.name: eval_use
items.role: use s { P }: the write rule of an agent reference, and from step 4 the context of the agent (AG-2).

items.name: MatcherState
items.role: The canonical state of a matcher capability (TR-5).

items.name: matcher_state_of
items.role: The state of a bare uppercase X id (MO-2).

items.name: MatcherProcess
items.role: The process MATCHER_OP (MO-1 to MO-4).

items.name: sink
items.role: The process SINK_OP (SK-1): it drops every message.
items.unmodeled: The sink has no effect, so no model state changes; its arity and remainder are pinned by the definition tests.

items.name: r7_route
items.role: The route of the produce of a system process: no context, and the bundle with both flags of an agent-minted name routes to its agent (R7A-1).

items.name: produce_agent_call
items.role: R7A-1: the Seq scan of the data and of raw, the persistent check, and the call of TS-1, produced again through the backend.

items.name: produce_call
items.role: The call A'!(sink, "produce", raw, [d...]) of a send on an agent space (TS-1, AG-4).
items.unmodeled: AgentSpaces.tla (P8 step 6, design v2 section 13) models the calls of a translation (RoutingIsolation, ReplayEquivalence). SpaceRefs.v models the route of the call (route with no context, AG-4).

items.name: route_send
items.role: T_send: the checks of TS-3, then the call routes as an ordinary send with no use-context (AG-4).
items.unmodeled: AgentSpaces.tla (P8 step 6, design v2 section 13) models the calls of a translation (RoutingIsolation, ReplayEquivalence). SpaceRefs.v models the route of the call (route with no context, AG-4).

items.name: route_send_from
items.role: The send loop of route_send from a given use-context: T_send turns an agent route into the call, which routes with no use-context (TS-1 to TS-3, AG-4). The call of a translated receive enters it with no use-context and with its data scanned (TR-7).
items.unmodeled: AgentSpaces.tla (P8 step 6, design v2 section 13) models the calls of a translation (RoutingIsolation, ReplayEquivalence). SpaceRefs.v models the route of the call (route with no context, AG-4).

items.name: dispatch_send
items.role: The operation of a routed send: the HEAD produce on the default space, or a produce on a collection of a native space.
items.unmodeled: A dispatch of a route that route_send_from computed: the HEAD produce or the space operation of the route, which the P4 and P5 maps model.

items.name: translate_receive
items.role: T_recv: the matcher receives, the body receive and the call of a receive on an agent space (TR-3 to TR-7).

items.name: offsets_of
items.role: The offsets and the total of the binds (TR-3).

items.name: place_guard
items.role: The owner bind of a guard (TR-4).

items.name: guard_indices
items.role: The free BoundVar indices of a guard by a charged walk with binder depth (TR-4).
items.unmodeled: AgentTranslation.v takes the indices of a guard as the section function indices; prop_guard_placement checks the walk against the BoundVars of generated guards.

items.name: body_pattern
items.role: The map pattern {"g": FreeVar(g)} of the body receive (TR-6).

items.name: env_forwarder
items.role: The body of a native consume that a translation describes: the env map to the body capability (HC-3).

items.name: consume_method
items.role: The handle method consume: strict matcher decode, HC-2, the read rule, and the native consume or join (W6).

items.name: describes_one_receive
items.role: HC-2: the matcher states describe one receive.
items.unmodeled: AgentSpaces.tla (P8 step 6, design v2 section 13) models the handle consume of a wrapper agent; the handle tests check each mismatch case of HC-2.

items.name: agent_consume
items.role: T_recv in the reducer: the Seq scan of the raw channels, the matcher receives, the body receive, and last the call on the agent (TR-7).
items.unmodeled: AgentTranslation.v models the terms that translate_receive builds (A3 to A8). AgentSpaces.tla (P8 step 6, design v2 section 13) models the order of the receives and the call (RoutingIsolation, ReplayEquivalence).

items.name: one_agent
items.role: TR-1: the one agent of a join whose channels all route to one user agent, by the equality of sorted references (AG-3), with each read reserved.
items.unmodeled: AgentSpaces.tla (P8 step 6, design v2 section 13) models the join rule of TR-1 (JoinSameSpace); reducer_space_routing_agent_join_and_mixes checks each mix.

items.name: agent_bind
items.role: The bind of a translated receive: the pattern and the raw channel of a bind that routes to a user agent.
items.unmodeled: A projection of a route of the model (RAgent a raw) into the bind that translate_receive takes; AgentTranslation.v models the translation of the binds.

items.name: reified_new
items.role: The hook of eval_new: in the context of an agent every plain binder is an agent binder and the new runs T_new; every other new allocates as before (W4, section 16).

items.name: agent_new
items.role: T_new: the draws of HEAD and the native allocation jobs (TN-1), P_closed in the wrapper of the context (TN-3), and the synthesized Par with no use-context (TN-4).

items.name: eval_new_space
items.role: new x : s in P: an annotation or a context of a user agent makes an agent binder, and a new with agent binders runs T_new (W4).

items.name: translate_new
items.role: T_new: the reply names (TN-2), the resume term (TN-3) and the gensym calls (TN-4).

items.name: agent_minted_name
items.role: The agent-minted name bundle{(AGENT_TAG, A, raw)} of a reply (TN-3).

items.name: levels_below
items.role: The bit set of the binder levels below a count: the locally_free set of a resume receive.
items.unmodeled: The models read no locally_free set (SpaceRefs.v, AgentTranslation.v); prop_resume_binds_innermost runs the substitution of the reducer, which recomputes the bit sets.
